Biliran’s Sangguniang Panlalawigan Launches Official Website to Drive Open Governance
Provincial Government of Biliran
•
News
NEWS

NAVAL, BILIRAN – The Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) of Biliran officially launched its new digital gateway during a ceremony at the Provincial Capitol, introducing an online platform engineered to bring legislative services closer to its constituents. Spearheaded by Vice Governor Roselyn Espina-Paras and members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, the initiative transitions the local legislative body into a digitally accessible space. The web platform serves as a central hub where citizens can view local ordinances, resolutions, committee activities, and legislative updates, aligning the province’s day-to-day operations with modern digital governance frameworks. The launch event highlighted the strategic role the platform plays in reshaping civic engagement and provincial administration. During his opening address, Honorable Brigido C. Caneja III emphasized the functional goals of the system, noting its capacity to build community partnerships. “This website serves as our platform to connect, share updates and bring public service closer to the people," Caneja remarked. "Through this website, we aim to promote just what we call, terms of use accountability, transparency and of course, meaningful public service by sharing programs, legislative updates and each of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan that matters in the Biliranon.” The web deployment complements the ongoing phase-in of the province’s broader structural modernization, which includes automated tracking mechanisms and a transition toward paperless workflows. In her keynote address, Vice Governor Espina-Paras framed the project as a vital bridge for open governance and environmental resource management. “Today marks another meaningful milestone for the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Biliran as we officially launch our official website — a platform that represents not only innovation, but also our commitment to transparency, accessibility, accountability, and environmental responsibility," Vice Governor Espina-Paras stated. "Through digitalization, we lessen paper consumption, reduce waste, and contribute in our own way toward environmental sustainability.”

Biliran Celebrates 34th Anniversary with Tribute to Unity and Excellence
NEWS

NAVAL, BILIRAN — The Province of Biliran marked its 34th Provincehood Anniversary on May 11, 2026, with a vibrant celebration at the Capitol Compound that showcased "Serbisyong Biliranon in Action." The festivities commenced with a thanksgiving mass and a grand parade, followed by an agri-tourism trade fair that brought together national government agencies, local government units, and civil society organizations. The event also featured the Biliranon Gawad Parangal, honoring the best among Biliranons and partners in local governance, alongside the A.L.A.G.A.D One-Stop Shop and specialized surgical missions at the Biliran Provincial Hospital. In his keynote address, Governor Rogelio Espina emphasized that the province’s growth is rooted in the sustained partnership of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, the eight municipalities, and the 132 barangays. “Itaguyod po natin ang walang humpay na kooperasyon at pagkakaisa upang lalo pa nating maiangat ang pamumuhay ng bawat pamilyang Biliran... Pangarap ko po na ang ating Mahal na Probinsya ay umangat mula 2nd class to FIRST CLASS Province,” the Governor stated. He further noted, “This milestone is more than a celebration of our provincehood; it is a reminder of how far we have come through unity and perseverance, and how much more we can achieve together for the future of every Biliranon.” Despite a simplified program due to a national energy emergency, the spirit of the celebration remained high as leaders reflected on the province’s journey of resilience. Vice Governor Roselyn Espina-Paras praised the collective strength of the people, remarking, “We proved that even a small province can stand tall when its people are united by purpose. When Biliranons come together, we rise together.” The day concluded with a heartfelt expression of gratitude to all sectors involved, setting a unified direction to build a more progressive and empowered community for generations to come.

Biliran Institutionalized “e-Legislation” to Modernize Sangguniang Panlalawigan
NEWS

NAVAL, BILIRAN – The Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Biliran has officially approved the "Biliran e-Legislation Ordinance," a policy move designed to transition the office toward a fully digital legislative process. Authored by Vice Governor Roselyn Espina-Paras, the ordinance institutionalizes a Paperless Session System and a Legislative Information System, aligning local operations with the Electronic Commerce Act of 2000. This shift replaces traditional, resource-intensive paper procedures with a streamlined electronic workflow that aims to enhance institutional efficiency and productivity across the Sangguniang Panlalawigan office. Under the new operating principles, all legislative documents—including the Order and Calendar of Business, Journals of Sessions, and Committee Reports—are to be converted into digital formats and distributed to board members via secure electronic channels. During sessions, these documents are projected on monitors for the provincial board and on a widescreen for the public gallery. This digital approach is intended to ensure that legislative proceedings are more transparent and easily accessible to visitors and guests, allowing the public to follow the development of local laws in real-time. To ensure the system's long-term sustainability, the ordinance establishes the SP Legislative Tracking and Monitoring Unit under the Office of the SP Secretary. This unit is tasked with managing a comprehensive database to track the status of proposed measures and monitor the implementation of enacted laws. Additionally, the ordinance provides for the creation of a Computer Operator position to oversee the system’s administration and mandates capacity-building training for all involved officials and staff. By integrating these technological advancements, the office of Sangguniang Panlalawigan reinforces its commitment to modern, accountable, and environmentally sustainable governance.

The Sanggunian Approved the Establishment of Sports Development Commission to Nurture Grassroots Talent
NEWS

NAVAL, BILIRAN – The Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the Province of Biliran has officially approved the "Biliran Sports Development Commission (BSDC) Ordinance of 2026," creating a unified body to oversee and elevate the province's athletic programs. Authored by Hon. Verne Symonn C. Roa and co-authored by Hon. Jose Antonio E. Paras, the measure addresses a long-standing gap in the local sports landscape by establishing a comprehensive and sustainable development plan. This commission will serve as the primary advisory and coordinating body for the province, integrating efforts from the provincial level down to every barangay to ensure a unified approach to athletic excellence. The ordinance is designed to act as a launchpad for young Biliranon athletes dreaming of regional, national, and international stages. By coordinating with the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) and the Department of Education (DepEd), the BSDC aims to better prepare local talents for high-level competitions like the EVRAA Meet, SCUAA, and Palarong Pambansa. Regarding the impact on the youth, Hon. Symonn Roa emphasized that "through this Commission, our young athletes will finally have the regional, national, and even international opportunities they truly deserve". This collaborative effort involves Municipal Governments, Barangay Local Government Units (BLGUs), and Sangguniang Kabataan Councils to ensure grassroots support. Beyond elite competition, the BSDC is tasked with fostering a culture of health and sportsmanship throughout the province by bringing development programs directly to local communities. The commission's functions include the potential establishment of a Provincial Sports Academy and the creation of sustainable incentives and recognition programs for winning athletes and coaches. Hon. Symonn Roa noted that "bringing sports in local communities will promote and foster health, unity, and sportsmanship across the entire province". By localizing these initiatives, the provincial government reinforces its commitment to youth empowerment and the development of a healthy, productive citizenry.

In a significant event marking the commencement of their public service, the newly elected officials of Biliran province, ranging from the Congressman to the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) members, participated in a mass oath-taking ceremony last May 15, 2025. The oaths were administered by Honorable Judge Luz P. Navarete, underscoring the solemnity and importance of the occasion. More than a formal rite, the ceremony symbolized unity and collective purpose among Biliran Province's elected leaders. It was a moment where public servants from the eight municipalities came together with a shared commitment to serve with integrity, uphold their constituents' trust, and work toward the common good of the province. This ceremony not only marks the beginning of a new chapter for Biliran's leadership but also reinforces the province's commitment to good governance and public service. As these officials step into their roles, they carry with them the hopes and support of the Biliranons, aiming to lead with transparency, accountability, and dedication.

Getting Here

Air-conditioned buses (Victory Liner, Florida Liner, etc.) bound for Cagayan Valley pass by the province. For independent motorists, take the North Luzon Expressway and exit at Sta. Rita. Nueva Vizcaya is accessible through the Cagayan Valley Road (Daang Maharlika) & is about 268 km north of Metro Manila (approximately 6-7 hrs of travel by land).

Alternative Route:

From NLEX, exit at SCTEX till you come to TPLEX. Exit at Victoria or Pura then head for San Jose City and Carranglan, Nueva Ecija until one reaches Sta. Fe, Nueva Vizcaya. Travel from Sta. Fe to the capital town of Bayombong is one(1 hour) only.

Via Air

Cauayan City Airport in Isabela is the nearest commercial airport to Nueva Vizcaya and is three hours by land. From the airport, one is highly recommended to hire services of a tourist van/ DOT accredited transport either the Nueva Vizcaya Transport Service Cooperative at 0906 268 0603 or the First Novo Vizcayano Travellers Cooperative at 0927 472 7417.

Getting Around

Public utility jeepneys ply the routes around the province. Tricycles are numerous in every town. Van/car rentals service are available with rates depending on the type vehicle used and the distance traveled.

I. MANDATE:

The Province of Dinagat Islands was created by virtue of Republic Act No. 9355 and signed into law on October 2, 2005 by Her Excellency Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, President of the Philippines.

The 5th province of Caraga Region and the 81st province of the Philippines is composed of seven (7) municipalities namely Basilisa, Cagdianao, Dinagat, Libjo (Albor), Loreto, San Jose and Tubajon and 100 barangays. Its population is 128, 117 based on the 2022 Census of Population. It is bounded on the NORTH, starting from the desolation point is Surigao Strait; on the EAST by the Philippine Sea; on the SOUTH by Gaboc Channel and Nonoc Island; on the SOUTH-WEST by Awasan Bay, Hanigad Island and Hikdop Island; and on the WEST by Surigao Strait.

The Province of Dinagat Islands contains an approximate land area of Eighty Thousand Two Hundred Twelve hectares (80,212 has.) or 802.12 sq. km. more or less including Hibusong Island and approximately two hundred fifty-four (254) islands and islets under the territorial jurisdiction of the municipalities. The capital town and seat of government of the Province of Dinagat Islands is the Municipality of San Jose.

The province has an independent and common seal and may alter the same at its pleasure. It shall exercise the powers to levy taxes; to close and open roads, streets, alleys, parks or squares; to take, purchase, receive, hold, lease, convey and dispose of real and personal property for the general interest of the province; to expropriate or condemn private property for public use; to contract and to be contracted with; to sue and to be sued; to prosecute and defend to final judgement and executions suits wherein the province is involved or interested in; and to exercise all the powers as are granted to corporations or hereafter granted.

The province was first led by the interim Governor Hon. Geraldine B. Ecleo-Villaroman from year 2007 to 2010. Then was followed by Hon. Glenda Buray-Ecleo as the second governor from year 2010 to 2019, who served for three (3) consecutive terms. In the 2019 election, Governor Arlene “Kaka” J. Bag-ao won and served as the third female Local Chief Executive from 2019-2022. On 2022 National and Local Elections Governor Nilo P. Demerey, Jr. then the Vice Governor won against Governor Arlene J. Bag-ao. He is the first male Governor and now serving his second term for year 2025-2028.

In 19 years of existence, the Province of Dinagat Islands continues to rise and showcases socioeconomic progress and development. With +9.6% growth rate of its Gross Domestic Product in 2024, the province is declared by the Philippine Statistics Authority as number 1 in Caraga Region, number 1 in Mindanao and number 3 fastest growing economy in the Philippines.

II. VISION

An industrialized agri-fishery and eco-tourism island province with responsively managed mining enjoyed by empowered, resilient, God centered and safe communities.

III. MISSION

The promotion of the general welfare of the people of Dinagat Islands is the primary mission of the Province. Towards this end, the Provincial Government shall endeavor to pursue sustainable development of its resources, including the protection of the environment, for a better quality of life of its citizenry, through good governance and effective partnerships with stakeholders and component LGUs.

IV. SERVICE PLEDGE

We, the officials and employees of the Provincial Government of Dinagat Islands, commit to provide efficient, transparent, and accountable public service consistent with our vision.

Guided by our mission, we pledge to:

Serve you promptly and courteously from Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM;
Provide accurate and updated information on our programs and services through:
Official Website: www.dinagatislands.gov.ph
Official Facebook page: www.facebook.com/PDIPIO
Attend to your needs immediately upon entering our office premises;
Ensure that our employees wear proper identification and deliver services with integrity, respect, and professionalism; and
Continuously improve our systems and processes in line with the REMEDY Strategic Development Framework TARGETS to ensure accessible, efficient, and quality public service for all.

Congreso General Ngobe Bugle
El Congreso General Ngobe Bugle es el espacio de participación social y democracia ciudadana de los pueblos originarios de la hoy comarca indígena Ngäbe-Buglé, en Panamá. Ha sido por más de 50 años el encuentro para el debate crítico y la reafirmación de la autodeterminación de los derechos colectivos y sociales y es reconocido por el Estado panameño mediante la Ley 10 del 7 de marzo de 1997.

Congreso General
Surge por iniciativa del los históricos líderes ngöbe que vieron la necesidad de construir espacios de análisis y propuestas para defender sus territorios frentes a los latifundios y proyectos estatales. En la etapa inicial de este proceso participan activamente personalidades como los caciques Camilo Ortega, Mónico Cruz, Lorenzo Rodriguez entre otros.

Antecedentes
Los Congresos Generales Ngobe Bugle desde su creación se convocan en las tres regiones comarcales (región Ño Kribo, región Nedrini y región Kodriri) como un espacio para la alternabilidad y continuidad democrática. Se convoca por derecho propio indígena, ya que los Congresos son entidades propiamente de los pueblos indígena de Panamá. Desde el surgimiento del Congreso General Ngoebe Bugle hasta 2011 se han efectuado XI congresos generales de manera tradicional, ya que esta es la única entidad organizativa del pueblo Ngobe y Bugle.

Actualidad
El XI Congreso se llevó a cabo en Pueblo Nuevo, Región Ño Kribo y en él fue electo como presidente el ingeniero Celio Guerra.

Indigenismo
Las comarcas indígenas de Panamá son cinco: Kuna Yala, Emberá-Wounaan, Kuna de Madungandí, Ngäbe-Buglé y Kuna de Wargandí; las cuales ocupan alrededor del 22.7% del territorio nacional /áreas boscosas, protegidas y de refugios de la bioderversidad. El Gobierno Nacional ha implementado políticas públicas tendientes a coadyuvar a mejorar las condiciones de vida personal, familiar y comunitaria de los pueblos indígenas.

POTENSI PROVINSI MALUKU
MINYAK DAN GAS
GAS BUMI, NIKEL, EMAS, MINYAK BUMI
Maluku merupakan salah satu provinsi di kawasan Timur Negara Republik Indonesia yang memiliki posisi strategis, karena kedudukannya berada antara sebagian wilayah Barat dan Tengah Indonesia dengan Papua di bagian Timur, serta menjadi penghubung wilayah Selatan yakni Negara Australia dan Timor Leste dengan wilayah Utara yaitu Maluku Utara dan Sulawesi. Selain itu, Provinsi Maluku berada pada jalur lintas internasional yaitu dilalui oleh 3 (tiga) Alur Laut Kepulaun Indonesia (ALKI). Posisi ini mempunyai arti yang sangat strategis di bidang ekonomi, perdagangan dan investasi.
